evidence_text: GitHub received a bug bounty report about this vulnerability from Wiz researchers on March 4, 2026.
source_excerpt: "On March 4, 2026, we received a vulnerability report through our Bug Bounty program from researchers at Wiz"
note:
The source attributes discovery and disclosure to Wiz through GitHub's Bug Bounty program.
```
caveat:

evidence_text: GitHub says the vulnerability affected github.com, GitHub Enterprise Cloud, GitHub Enterprise Cloud with Data Residency, GitHub Enterprise Cloud with Enterprise Managed Users, and GitHub Enterprise Server.
source_excerpt: The report described "a critical remote code execution vulnerability affecting github.com, GitHub Enterprise Cloud, GitHub Enterprise Cloud with Data Residency, GitHub Enterprise Cloud with Enterprise Managed Users, and GitHub Enterprise Server."
note:
This evidence is the source's stated affected-product scope.
```
caveat:
This evidence is the source's stated affected-product scope.
```

evidence_text: The reported attack required only a single git push command with a crafted push option using an unsanitized character.
source_excerpt: "The attack required only a single command: git push with a crafted push option that leveraged an unsanitized character."
note:
This is the source's description of exploit simplicity, not an independent reproduction record.
```
caveat:
This is the source's description of exploit simplicity, not an independent reproduction record.
```

evidence_text: GitHub says it reproduced the vulnerability internally within 40 minutes and confirmed it was critical.
source_excerpt: "Within 40 minutes, we had reproduced the vulnerability internally and confirmed the severity. This was a critical issue"
note:
This is a response-timing and severity claim from GitHub's account.
```
caveat:
This is a response-timing and severity claim from GitHub's account.
```

evidence_text: User-supplied git push option values were inserted into internal metadata without sufficient sanitization.
source_excerpt: "the values provided by the user were incorporated into the internal metadata without sufficient sanitization."
note:
This is part of the source's root-cause description.
```
caveat:
This is part of the source's root-cause description.
```

evidence_text: Because the internal metadata format used a delimiter character that could also appear in user input, an attacker could inject additional fields that downstream services treated as trusted internal values.
source_excerpt: "Because the internal metadata format used a delimiter character that could also appear in user input, an attacker could inject additional fields that the downstream service would interpret as trusted internal values."
note:
This evidence states the injection mechanism as described in the source.
```
caveat:
This evidence states the injection mechanism as described in the source.
```

evidence_text: The researchers demonstrated that chained injected values could override the push-processing environment, bypass sandboxing protections, and execute arbitrary commands on the server.
source_excerpt: "By chaining several injected values together, the researchers demonstrated that an attacker could override the environment the push was processed in, bypass sandboxing protections that normally constrain hook execution, and ultimately execute arbitrary commands on the server."
note:
This is the source's described exploit chain and impact.
```
caveat:
This is the source's described exploit chain and impact.
```

evidence_text: GitHub says it identified the root cause at 5:45 p.m. UTC on March 4, 2026, and deployed a fix to github.com at 7:00 p.m. UTC the same day.
source_excerpt: "With the root cause identified on March, 4, 2026, at 5:45 p.m. UTC, our engineering team developed and deployed a fix to github.com at 7:00 p.m. UTC that same day."
note:
This evidence captures the reported remediation timeline.
```
caveat:
This evidence captures the reported remediation timeline.
```

evidence_text: GitHub says the fix prevents user-supplied push option values from influencing internal metadata fields by sanitizing them properly.
source_excerpt: "The fix ensures that user-supplied push option values are properly sanitized and can no longer influence internal metadata fields."
note:
This is the source's stated primary remediation.
```

This is the source's stated primary remediation.

evidence_text: GitHub says the exploit necessarily triggered an anomalous server code path that is never used during normal github.com operations.
source_excerpt: "The exploit forces the server to take a code path that is never used during normal operations on github.com. This is not something an attacker can avoid or suppress"
note:
This evidence matters to the forensic claim because GitHub presents the anomalous code path as a reliable detection condition.
```
caveat:

source_excerpt: "Every occurrence mapped to the Wiz researchers’ own testing activity. No other users or accounts triggered this code path."

This is a source-reported forensic result based on telemetry queries.

source_excerpt: "No customer data was accessed, modified, or exfiltrated as a result of this vulnerability."
note:

```

evidence_text: The exploit worked in part because a code path not intended for that environment still existed on disk in the server container image after a deployment-model change failed to preserve an older exclusion.
source_excerpt: "This code path existed on disk as part of the server’s container image, even though it was only meant to be used in a different product configuration. An older deployment method had correctly excluded this code, but when the deployment model changed, the exclusion was not carried forward."
note:
This introduces a defense-in-depth gap beyond the input-sanitization bug and should remain attached as a caveat about environment hardening.
```
caveat:
This introduces a defense-in-depth gap beyond the input-sanitization bug and should remain attached as a caveat about environment hardening.
```

evidence_text: For GHES, the source says exploitation requires an authenticated user with push access, and administrators are advised to review /var/log/github-audit.log for push operations containing a semicolon in push options.
source_excerpt: "For GHES customers, exploitation would require an authenticated user with push access on your instance." and "We recommend that you review /var/log/github-audit.log for push operations containing ; in push options."
note: This is scoped specifically to GHES and is operational guidance rather than proof of observed exploitation on customer instances.
caveat: This is scoped specifically to GHES and is operational guidance rather than proof of observed exploitation on customer instances.
